obligations.note: The change adds `if payee.category == "tax_authority": continue` to purge_due (scope path apps/baseline-payments/payments/retention.py). Closed tax-authority payees past the retention period, and not on legal hold, never have their NPI (holder name, account/routing number, tax ID) purged. RET-1 allows only legal hold as an exception. The passing control test only checks sampled vendor payees, so it does not catch this.

The deviation from RET-1 is not covered by any exception: the register holds only EXC-0141 (SES-1, expired 2026-09-15), EXC-0167 (LOG-1, mortgage.logging) and EXC-0172 (MFA-1, withdrawn). None is scoped to RET-1 or payments.retention.

Ticket CHG-25709 is standard and was approved on 2026-10-09 by Erik Brandt (change_manager), before the change was opened and reviewed. Its components [payments.retention] cover the only touched file, retention.py.
Code review approval from mara.costa@fernbrook.example, a payments change_approver who is a different person from the author Linh Nguyen (p-lnguyen).
The approval names head commit be74efa, which is the change's only commit, so no later commits exist.

records/ci/run.json shows ci/run-tests.sh baseline-payments succeeded on head be74efa. The JUnit report has 172 tests, 0 failures and 0 skips, including the RET-1 control test test_sampled_purge_respects_hold (labelled sample). I could not rerun it locally because pytest is not installed.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers retention.py or the other RET-1 scope symbols, so no prior evidence lapses because of this change.

summary: PR-1270 makes the payments retention job skip closed tax-authority payees, so their NPI is never disposed of after the approved retention period even without a legal hold. That directly violates RET-1, and no approved, unexpired RET-1 exception exists in the register. The process checks are satisfied: the approved ticket covers the component, the independent code review names the head commit, and CI on the head commit passed. The RET-1 control test is sample-based and does not exercise tax-authority payees, so its pass does not show compliance. The change is rejected.
